name: theotokos

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Dogmatic Definition of the Council of Ephesus

VINIT.justification: The unmanifest state of the promise before the specific historical intervention of the Word.

TANCH.justification: The final doctrinal boundary that secures the identity of the Mother as the God-bearer.

AFWD.justification: The forward movement of human consent toward the divine invitation.

AREV.justification: The descent of the Logos into the womb, a reverse morphism from infinite to finite.

CLINK.justification: The sequential chaining of divine grace and human will to produce the Incarnation.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-contained identity of the vessel that remains itself before, during, and after the event.

FSPLIT.justification: The differentiation of the single person of Christ into divine and human natures.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the two natures into the single person of the Word.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative response and celebration of the fulfilled promise.

EVALF.justification: The experience of the negative branch, the suffering at the foot of the cross.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Mater Dolorosa et Causa Nostrae Laetitiae
ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous holding of sorrow and joy in the person of Mary.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, irreversible fixation of the body and soul into the eternal state.

phase_3.void_description: The state of the world before the Incarnation, awaiting the fulfillment of the protoevangelium.
phase_3.true_description: The state of grace and the realization of the divine presence in the flesh.
phase_3.false_description: The state of death and the apparent defeat of the promise during the Passion.
phase_3.both_description: The mystery of the Theotokos, where a finite creature contains the infinite Creator.

steps.domain_action: The silence of the Old Covenant awaits the fulfillment of the promise.
The Virgin is identified as the chosen vessel, set apart in her own identity.
The Archangel Gabriel proposes the divine plan to the Virgin.
The proposal branches into the possibility of human acceptance or refusal.
The Virgin utters her Fiat, providing the affirmative human consent.
The divine will and human will unite to initiate the conception.
The Logos descends into the womb, taking on the limitations of human flesh.
The biological and spiritual processes chain together to form the God-man.
The identity of the Mother is transformed into the Theotokos.
The conception is recorded as an irreversible event in salvation history.
The life of the Son branches into the public ministry and the hidden life.
The wedding at Cana marks the first public sign and the Mother's intercession.
The prophecy of Simeon regarding the sword piercing the soul is realized at Calvary.
At the Cross, the Mother holds the death of her Son and the birth of the Church simultaneously.
The Resurrection reunites the suffering and the glory into a single reality.
The Assumption permanently fixes the Theotokos in the heavenly realm.
The Council of Ephesus formally seals the definition of the God-bearer for all time.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Holy Spirit, who overshadows the Virgin to translate the Word into flesh.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Prayer and intercession, the communication channels between the Mother and the Son.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Sacred Tradition and Scripture, which store the record of the Marian events.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The Fullness of Time, which determines the precise moment of the Incarnation.
phase_5.alfs_store: The Protoevangelium in Genesis, the original bootstrap promise for the Theotokos.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The kenotic emptying of the Logos and the sacrificial consent of the Virgin.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A world separated from the immediate presence of the incarnate God.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A world where the divine and human are permanently united in the person of Christ.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The infinite nature of the Logos ensures that the descent into finitude does not deplete the divine source.
